title: 湖北古建筑地图 - 术语数据库
title_en: Historical Architectural Map of Hubei - Terminology Database

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑特有的承重构件，由方形斗、弓形拱和斜向昂层层叠叠组合而成，位于柱顶与梁枋、屋顶之间，将屋顶荷载传递到柱子上，同时具有装饰作用。
terms.definition_en: A unique load-bearing component of traditional Chinese architecture, composed of square dou (blocks), bow-shaped gong (arms), and ang (levers) stacked in layers, located between column tops and beams/roofs, transferring roof loads to columns while also serving a decorative function.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑屋顶形式之一，由一条正脊、四条垂脊和四条戗脊组成，上部为悬山式，下部为庑殿式，又称九脊顶，常用于宫殿、寺庙的次要建筑。
terms.definition_en: One of the traditional Chinese roof forms, consisting of one main ridge, four vertical ridges, and four diagonal ridges; the upper part is of the overhanging-gable type and the lower part of the hip type, also called the nine-ridge roof, commonly used for secondary buildings of palaces and temples.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑最常见的屋顶形式之一，屋面仅有前后两坡，左右两侧山墙与屋面齐平或略高于屋面，结构简单，多用于民居和普通建筑。
terms.definition_en: One of the most common roof forms in traditional Chinese architecture, with only front and rear slopes; the left and right gable walls are flush with or slightly higher than the roof surface, with a simple structure, mostly used for residences and ordinary buildings.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑屋顶形式之一，屋面有前后两坡，且屋面伸出山墙之外，形成悬挑，有利于保护山墙免受雨水侵蚀，多用于民居。
terms.definition_en: One of the traditional Chinese roof forms, with front and rear slopes that extend beyond the gable walls, forming an overhang that helps protect the gable walls from rain erosion, mostly used for residences.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑最高等级的屋顶形式，由一条正脊和四条垂脊组成，屋面有四坡，又称四阿顶，仅用于宫殿、寺庙的主殿等最高等级建筑。
terms.definition_en: The highest-grade roof form in traditional Chinese architecture, consisting of one main ridge and four vertical ridges, with four roof slopes, also called the four-eave roof, used only for the highest-grade buildings such as main halls of palaces and temples.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑屋顶形式之一，屋面为锥形，顶部集中于一点（宝顶），无正脊，有三角、四角、六角、八角和圆形等多种形式，常用于亭、阁、塔。
terms.definition_en: One of the traditional Chinese roof forms, with a conical roof surface converging at a single point (finial) at the top, without a main ridge; available in triangular, quadrangular, hexagonal, octagonal, and circular forms, commonly used for pavilions, towers, and pagodas.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中一种高等级的台基形式，源于佛教须弥山的意象，由多层线脚组成，上下出涩、中间束腰，常用于宫殿、寺庙的主殿和重要建筑。
terms.definition_en: A high-grade pedestal form in traditional Chinese architecture, derived from the imagery of Mount Sumeru in Buddhism, composed of multiple moldings, with protruding upper and lower parts and a concave central waist, commonly used for main halls and important buildings of palaces and temples.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中一种高级屋面材料，以陶土为胎，表面施铅釉烧制而成，色彩丰富（黄、绿、蓝、黑等），防水性好，光泽亮丽，用于宫殿、寺庙等高等级建筑。
terms.definition_en: A high-grade roofing material in traditional Chinese architecture, made of clay body with lead glaze fired on the surface, with rich colors (yellow, green, blue, black, etc.), good waterproofing, and bright luster, used for high-grade buildings such as palaces and temples.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑主要结构体系之一，在柱础上立柱，柱上架梁，梁上再立短柱、架梁，层层叠叠，形成屋架，多用于北方官式建筑和大型殿堂。
terms.definition_en: One of the main structural systems of traditional Chinese architecture, with columns erected on column bases, beams placed on columns, short columns and beams further placed on beams, stacked in layers to form the roof truss, mostly used for northern official-style buildings and large halls.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑主要结构体系之一，以柱直接承檩，柱间用穿枋串联，形成整体框架，用料较省，多用于南方民居和中小型建筑。
terms.definition_en: One of the main structural systems of traditional Chinese architecture, with columns directly supporting purlins and columns connected by tie beams to form an integral frame, using less material, mostly used for southern residences and small-to-medium buildings.

terms.definition_zh: 中国南方民居特有的山墙形式，山墙高出屋面，呈阶梯状或云形，因形似马头而得名，具有防火（封火墙）和装饰作用，常见于徽派和鄂东南民居。
terms.definition_en: A gable wall form unique to southern Chinese residences, with the gable wall rising above the roof in stepped or cloud shapes, named for its resemblance to a horse head; it has fire-prevention (fire-sealing wall) and decorative functions, commonly seen in Huizhou-style and southeastern Hubei residences.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中硬山建筑山墙伸出檐柱之外的部分，通常有 elaborate 的砖雕装饰，是建筑立面的重要装饰部位。
terms.definition_en: In traditional Chinese architecture, the part of the gable wall of a gable building that extends beyond the eave columns, usually with elaborate brick carving decoration, serving as an important decorative element of the building facade.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中置于大门两侧的石雕构件，下部为须弥座，上部为圆鼓形，具有固定门枕和装饰作用，是门第等级的象征。
terms.definition_en: A stone-carved component placed on both sides of the main gate in traditional Chinese architecture, with a Sumeru pedestal at the bottom and a round drum shape at the top, serving to fix the door pillow and for decoration, symbolizing the rank of the household.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中一种装饰性很强的门，由外框、格心和裙板组成，格心有各种棂花图案，常用于宫殿、寺庙、民居的正立面。
terms.definition_en: A highly decorative door in traditional Chinese architecture, composed of an outer frame, lattice core, and skirt board, with various lattice patterns on the lattice core, commonly used on the front facades of palaces, temples, and residences.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中一种标志性、纪念性建筑，由立柱、额枋、斗拱和楼顶组成，有木、石、琉璃等多种材质，用于街道、庙宇、陵墓入口处。
terms.definition_en: A landmark and commemorative building in traditional Chinese architecture, composed of columns, architraves, bracket sets, and roof tops, available in wood, stone, glazed, and other materials, used at the entrances of streets, temples, and tombs.

terms.definition_zh: 中国乡土建筑中一种防御性高层建筑，通常为砖石结构，墙上开有射击孔和瞭望窗，用于防御盗贼和战乱，常见于鄂西北、广东等地。
terms.definition_en: A defensive high-rise building in Chinese vernacular architecture, usually of brick-stone structure, with shooting holes and lookout windows on the walls, used for defense against bandits and war turmoil, commonly seen in northwestern Hubei, Guangdong, and other places.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中一种防御性建筑，墙上开有箭孔（射击孔），用于防御和瞭望，常与城墙、城门配合使用。
terms.definition_en: A defensive building in traditional Chinese architecture, with arrow holes (shooting holes) opened on the walls, used for defense and lookout, often used in conjunction with city walls and city gates.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代为调节风水、振兴文运而建的塔，多为楼阁式砖塔，常建于城镇东南方或山水交汇处，具有象征意义。
terms.definition_en: Pagodas built in ancient China to regulate fengshui and revitalize literary fortune, mostly pavilion-style brick pagodas, often built southeast of towns or at the confluence of mountains and rivers, with symbolic significance.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古塔中最常见的形式之一，仿木结构楼阁，分层设塔身、塔檐和平座，可登临眺望，有砖、木、石等多种结构。
terms.definition_en: One of the most common forms of ancient Chinese pagodas, imitating wooden-structure pavilions, with tower body, eaves, and balconies set in layers, climbable for overlooking, available in brick, wood, stone, and other structures.

terms.definition_zh: 中国西南少数民族地区特有的民居形式，房屋架于木桩之上，底层架空，适应山地地形和潮湿气候，常见于土家族、苗族等地区。
terms.definition_en: A residential form unique to ethnic minority areas in southwestern China, with the house built on wooden piles and the ground floor elevated, adapting to mountain terrain and humid climate, commonly seen in Tujia, Miao, and other ethnic areas.

terms.definition_zh: 中国西南少数民族地区土司（世袭地方首领）的统治中心，集官署、住宅、宗庙、军事设施于一体，反映土司制度的政治文化。
terms.definition_en: The ruling center of tusi (hereditary local chiefs) in ethnic minority areas of southwestern China, integrating government offices, residences, ancestral temples, and military facilities, reflecting the political culture of the tusi system.

terms.definition_zh: 土家族特有的祭祀和歌舞场所，用于祭祀祖先和跳摆手舞，是土家族文化的重要载体。
terms.definition_en: A sacrificial and song-and-dance venue unique to the Tujia people, used for ancestor worship and the hand-waving dance, serving as an important carrier of Tujia culture.

terms.definition_zh: 中国西南少数民族地区特有的桥梁形式，桥上建廊屋，可供行人避雨休息，兼具交通、祭祀和社交功能。
terms.definition_en: A bridge form unique to ethnic minority areas in southwestern China, with corridor houses built on the bridge for pedestrians to take shelter from rain and rest, integrating transportation, sacrifice, and social functions.

terms.definition_zh: 中国传统社会中宗族祭祀祖先、议事和举办礼仪活动的场所，是宗族制度的物质载体，建筑规格和装饰反映宗族的地位和财力。
terms.definition_en: In traditional Chinese society, a place for clans to worship ancestors, discuss affairs, and hold ceremonial activities, serving as the material carrier of the clan system; the architectural specifications and decorations reflect the clan status and financial resources.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代特有的教育机构，集教学、藏书、祭祀于一体，建筑多为院落式布局，有讲堂、藏书楼、祭祀殿等。
terms.definition_en: An educational institution unique to ancient China, integrating teaching, book collection, and sacrifice, mostly with a courtyard-style layout, including lecture halls, book storage towers, and sacrificial halls.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代祭祀孔子的礼制建筑，也是地方官学的所在地，通常有大成殿、明伦堂、泮池、棂星门等建筑。
terms.definition_en: A ritual building in ancient China for sacrificing to Confucius, also the location of local official schools, usually with Dacheng Hall, Minglun Hall, Pan Pond, and Lingxing Gate.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代同乡或同业商人在异地建立的组织和建筑，集聚会、祭祀、住宿、商业活动于一体，建筑装饰往往极为精美。
terms.definition_en: Organizations and buildings established in other places by fellow townsmen or same-trade merchants in ancient China, integrating gatherings, sacrifice, accommodation, and commercial activities; the architectural decorations are often extremely exquisite.

terms.definition_zh: 18-19世纪西方流行的建筑风格，复兴古希腊罗马建筑元素，如柱式、山花、拱券，追求庄重、对称和秩序，汉口近代建筑群中大量采用。
terms.definition_en: An architectural style popular in the West in the 18th-19th centuries, reviving ancient Greek and Roman architectural elements such as orders, pediments, and arches, pursuing solemnity, symmetry, and order; extensively used in the Hankou modern building complex.

terms.definition_zh: 14-17世纪欧洲文艺复兴时期的建筑风格，强调古典柱式、对称构图、水平线条和拱券，汉口近代建筑中有较多体现。
terms.definition_en: The architectural style of the European Renaissance period (14th-17th centuries), emphasizing classical orders, symmetrical composition, horizontal lines, and arches, with many manifestations in Hankou modern architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 17-18世纪欧洲流行的建筑风格，特征是动态的曲线、华丽的装饰、强烈的光影对比和戏剧性效果，汉口部分近代建筑受其影响。
terms.definition_en: An architectural style popular in Europe in the 17th-18th centuries, characterized by dynamic curves, ornate decoration, strong light-shadow contrast, and dramatic effects; some modern buildings in Hankou were influenced by it.

terms.definition_zh: 近代建筑中以钢筋和混凝土组合而成的结构体系，强度高、防火性好、可塑型强，是20世纪初高层建筑的主要结构形式。
terms.definition_en: A structural system in modern architecture combining steel reinforcement and concrete, with high strength, good fire resistance, and strong moldability, serving as the main structural form of high-rise buildings in the early 20th century.

terms.definition_zh: 中国传统建筑装饰工艺之一，在青砖上雕刻人物、花卉、鸟兽等图案，常用于门楼、墀头、影壁等部位，徽派和鄂东南建筑尤为发达。
terms.definition_en: One of the traditional Chinese architectural decoration crafts, carving figures, flowers, birds, and beasts on blue bricks, commonly used for gate towers, gable ends, and screen walls; particularly developed in Huizhou-style and southeastern Hubei architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 中国传统建筑装饰工艺之一，在木构件上雕刻各种图案，有浮雕、透雕、圆雕等技法，常用于梁枋、门窗、斜撑等部位。
terms.definition_en: One of the traditional Chinese architectural decoration crafts, carving various patterns on wooden components, with techniques such as relief, openwork, and round carving, commonly used for beams, doors and windows, and diagonal braces.

terms.definition_zh: 中国传统建筑装饰工艺之一，在石材上雕刻各种图案，有线刻、浮雕、圆雕、透雕等技法，常用于牌坊、抱鼓石、柱础、栏杆等部位。
terms.definition_en: One of the traditional Chinese architectural decoration crafts, carving various patterns on stone, with techniques such as line carving, relief, round carving, and openwork, commonly used for archways, drum-holding stones, column bases, and railings.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代以铜铸造、表面鎏金的殿堂，是最高等级的金属建筑，武当山金殿为明代铜铸鎏金建筑的代表。
terms.definition_en: In ancient China, a hall cast in bronze and gilded on the surface, representing the highest grade of metal architecture; the Wudang Mountain Golden Hall is a representative of Ming Dynasty bronze-cast gilded architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代以铜铸造的仿木构殿堂，构件在外地铸造后运至现场拼装，是金属建筑的特殊形式，武当山转运殿内的铜殿为元代铸造。
terms.definition_en: In ancient China, an imitation-wood hall cast in bronze, with components cast elsewhere and transported to the site for assembly, a special form of metal architecture; the bronze hall inside the Wudang Transport Hall was cast in the Yuan Dynasty.

terms.definition_zh: 本指北京皇宫，此处指武当山天柱峰上环绕金顶的石砌城墙，因象征天帝居所而得名，是武当山最高等级的建筑区域。
terms.definition_en: Originally referring to the Beijing imperial palace, here it refers to the stone-built city wall surrounding the Golden Summit on Tianzhu Peak of Wudang Mountain, named for symbolizing the residence of the Heavenly Emperor; it is the highest-grade architectural area of Wudang Mountain.

terms.definition_zh: 武当山古建筑群中九座重要道观的合称，包括太玄观、元和观、复真观、回龙观、仁威观、威烈观、八仙观、龙泉观、太常观，是武当山道教建筑体系的重要组成部分。
terms.definition_en: The collective name for nine important Taoist temples in the Wudang Mountain ancient building complex, including Taixuan Temple, Yuanhe Temple, Fuzhen Temple, Huilong Temple, Renwei Temple, Weilie Temple, Baxian Temple, Longquan Temple, and Taichang Temple, serving as an important part of the Wudang Taoist architectural system.

terms.definition_zh: 武当山古建筑群中八座重要宫殿的合称，包括净乐宫、迎恩宫、玉虚宫、遇真宫、紫霄宫、南岩宫、太和宫、五龙宫，是武当山道教建筑的核心。
terms.definition_en: The collective name for eight important palaces in the Wudang Mountain ancient building complex, including Jingle Palace, Ying'en Palace, Yuxu Palace, Yuzhen Palace, Zixiao Palace, Nanyan Palace, Taihe Palace, and Wulong Palace, serving as the core of Wudang Taoist architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 通向寺庙、陵墓等神圣场所的道路，通常有严格的轴线和序列，两侧可能有石像生、牌坊等，武当山神道从山脚延伸至金顶。
terms.definition_en: A road leading to sacred places such as temples and tombs, usually with a strict axis and sequence, possibly with stone statues and archways on both sides; the Wudang Mountain sacred path extends from the foot of the mountain to the Golden Summit.

terms.definition_zh: 武当山神道上的标志性建筑，象征从人间进入天界的入口，有一天门、二天门、三天门等，均为砖石拱券门。
terms.definition_en: A landmark building on the Wudang Mountain sacred path, symbolizing the entrance from the human world to the heavenly realm, including the First, Second, and Third Heaven Gates, all of which are brick-stone arched gates.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中位于大门内外的墙壁，用于遮挡视线和装饰，有砖雕、琉璃等多种形式，又称照壁。
terms.definition_en: A wall located inside or outside the main gate in traditional Chinese architecture, used to block the view and for decoration, available in brick carving, glazed, and other forms, also called zhaobi.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中大门两侧呈八字形展开的墙壁，具有扩大入口气势和引导人流的作用，常用于祠堂、庙宇和官署。
terms.definition_en: In traditional Chinese architecture, walls splayed in a figure-eight shape on both sides of the main gate, serving to enhance the imposing presence of the entrance and guide pedestrian flow, commonly used for ancestral halls, temples, and government offices.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑屋顶形式之一，屋面双坡相交处不设正脊，呈弧形曲面，外观柔和，多用于园林建筑和配殿。
terms.definition_en: One of the traditional Chinese roof forms, with no main ridge at the intersection of the two roof slopes, presenting an arc-shaped curved surface with a soft appearance, mostly used for garden buildings and side halls.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中屋檐有上下两层的做法，增加建筑的高度和庄重感，用于高等级建筑的主殿。
terms.definition_en: In traditional Chinese architecture, the practice of having two layers of eaves (upper and lower), increasing the height and solemnity of the building, used for the main halls of high-grade buildings.
examples: 文庙大成殿重檐歇山顶

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑屋脊两端的装饰构件，形似龙首鱼身，传说能喷水灭火，具有镇火和装饰作用。
terms.definition_en: Decorative components at both ends of the roof ridge in traditional Chinese architecture, shaped like a dragon head with a fish body; legend says they can spray water to extinguish fires, serving fire-suppression and decorative functions.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑屋脊上的装饰构件，最前端为骑凤仙人，其后依次排列龙、凤、狮子、天马、海马等走兽，数量和种类反映建筑等级。
terms.definition_en: Decorative components on the roof ridges of traditional Chinese architecture, with an immortal riding a phoenix at the front, followed by beasts such as dragon, phoenix, lion, heavenly horse, and sea horse in sequence; the number and type reflect the building grade.

terms.definition_zh: 中国南方民居中特有的院落形式，四面房屋围合，中间为小天井，用于采光、通风和排水，适应南方湿热气候。
terms.definition_en: A courtyard form unique to southern Chinese residences, with houses on all sides enclosing a small central courtyard for lighting, ventilation, and drainage, adapting to the hot and humid southern climate.

terms.definition_zh: 鄂西北一带对装饰精美的大型民居的称呼，通常有精美的木雕、砖雕和石雕，是当地富商和乡绅的豪宅。
terms.definition_en: A term in northwestern Hubei for large residences with exquisite decorations, usually with fine wood, brick, and stone carvings, serving as mansions of local wealthy merchants and gentry.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代地主和富商的大型住宅建筑群，集居住、防御、生产于一体，通常有围墙、碉楼和多进院落。
terms.definition_en: Large residential building complexes of ancient Chinese landlords and wealthy merchants, integrating residence, defense, and production, usually with enclosing walls, watchtowers, and multiple courtyards.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代城市的防御设施，由墙体、城门、城楼、瓮城、护城河等组成，是城市历史和军事技术的实物见证。
terms.definition_en: Defensive facilities of ancient Chinese cities, composed of walls, city gates, gate towers, barbican entrances, and moats, serving as physical witnesses to urban history and military technology.

terms.definition_zh: 环绕城市的人工河道，用于防御和排水，是古城防御体系的重要组成部分。
terms.definition_en: An artificial waterway surrounding a city, used for defense and drainage, serving as an important part of the ancient city defense system.

terms.definition_zh: 以砖石砌筑的弧形门洞，结构稳固，跨度较大，常用于城门、塔门和重要建筑入口。
terms.definition_en: An arc-shaped gate opening built of brick and stone, with a stable structure and large span, commonly used for city gates, pagoda gates, and important building entrances.

terms.definition_zh: 以石、砖、铜等材料模仿木结构建筑的形制和构件，如仿木斗拱、仿木梁枋，常见于石牌坊、铜殿和砖石塔。
terms.definition_en: Using stone, brick, bronze, and other materials to imitate the form and components of wooden-structure buildings, such as imitation-wood bracket sets and beams, commonly seen in stone archways, bronze halls, and brick-stone pagodas.
examples: 治世玄岳牌坊仿木式样

terms.definition_zh: 建筑表面的凹凸线条装饰，用于台基、柱础、额枋等部位，增加层次感和装饰性。
terms.definition_en: Concave-convex line decorations on building surfaces, used for pedestals, column bases, architraves, and other parts, increasing layering and decorativeness.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古建筑中在木构件表面绘制的彩色图案，有和玺、旋子、苏式等种类，兼具保护木材和装饰作用。
terms.definition_en: Colorful patterns painted on the surface of wooden components in traditional Chinese architecture, with types such as Hexi, Xuanzi, and Suzhou styles, serving both to protect wood and for decoration.

terms.definition_zh: 绘制在墙壁上的图画，中国古代寺庙、祠堂和墓葬中常见，内容多为宗教故事、历史人物和吉祥图案。
terms.definition_en: Pictures painted on walls, common in ancient Chinese temples, ancestral halls, and tombs, with content mostly religious stories, historical figures, and auspicious patterns.
examples: 彭家祠堂二十四孝壁画

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代二十四个孝子故事的合称，是儒家孝道思想的通俗化表达，常见于祠堂、民居的壁画和雕刻。
terms.definition_en: The collective name for twenty-four stories of filial sons in ancient China, a popularized expression of Confucian filial piety thought, commonly seen in murals and carvings of ancestral halls and residences.
examples: 彭家祠堂二十四孝壁画

terms.definition_zh: 中国民间传说中八位神仙各显神通渡海的故事，是传统建筑装饰中常见的吉祥题材。
terms.definition_en: A Chinese folk tale about eight immortals each showing their divine powers to cross the sea, a common auspicious theme in traditional architectural decoration.
examples: 饶氏庄园木雕八仙过海

terms.term_en: Five Blessings Arriving at the Door
terms.definition_zh: 中国传统吉祥语，五福指长寿、富贵、康宁、好德、善终，常以五只蝙蝠图案象征，用于建筑装饰。
terms.definition_en: A traditional Chinese auspicious phrase; the five blessings refer to longevity, wealth, health, virtue, and a peaceful death, often symbolized by five bat patterns in architectural decoration.
examples: 饶氏庄园五只蝙蝠雕刻

terms.definition_zh: 中国传统吉祥图案，以猴子骑在马上象征马上封侯，寓意仕途顺利、加官进爵。
terms.definition_en: A traditional Chinese auspicious pattern, symbolizing immediate conferment as a marquis by a monkey riding a horse, meaning smooth official career and promotion.
examples: 饶氏庄园小猴子拴马桩

terms.term_en: Purple Qi Comes from the East
terms.definition_zh: 中国传统吉祥语，源自老子出函谷关的传说，象征祥瑞降临，常用于大门匾额。
terms.definition_en: A traditional Chinese auspicious phrase, derived from the legend of Laozi leaving Hangu Pass, symbolizing the arrival of auspiciousness, commonly used for gate plaques.
examples: 上庸古建筑群紫气东来石匾

terms.definition_zh: 春秋时期鲁国的能工巧匠，被后世尊为木匠和建筑业的祖师爷，民间有许多关于他显圣助建的传说。
terms.definition_en: A skilled craftsman of the State of Lu in the Spring and Autumn period, revered by later generations as the patriarch of carpenters and the construction industry; there are many folk legends about him manifesting his divine power to help construction.

terms.definition_zh: 道教尊奉的北方之神，又称玄天上帝、玄武大帝，武当山为其道场，是武当山道教建筑的核心信仰对象。
terms.definition_en: The god of the north revered in Taoism, also called the Mysterious Heaven Emperor or the Great Emperor Xuanwu; Wudang Mountain is his sacred site, serving as the core object of belief in Wudang Taoist architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 中国古代一种救灾制度，政府在灾年招募灾民从事工程建设，以工钱代替直接救济，既救济灾民又完成工程。
terms.definition_en: An ancient Chinese disaster relief system in which the government recruited disaster victims to engage in engineering construction in famine years, using wages instead of direct relief, both relieving victims and completing projects.
examples: 治世玄岳牌坊以工代赈修建

terms.definition_zh: 明永乐十年（1412），明成祖朱棣为报答真武大帝庇佑，动用大量人力物力大修武当山，建成八宫九观等庞大建筑群，是武当山建筑史上最重要的事件。
terms.definition_en: In the 10th year of Yongle, Ming (1412), Emperor Chengzu Zhu Di, to repay the protection of the Great Emperor Zhenwu, used a large amount of manpower and material resources to carry out a major renovation of Wudang Mountain, building a庞大 building complex including eight palaces and nine temples; it is the most important event in the architectural history of Wudang Mountain.

terms.definition_zh: 明嘉靖三十一年（1552），嘉靖皇帝为崇信道教，再次大修武当山，建治世玄岳牌坊，维修八宫庙观，是武当山建筑史上第二次大规模建设。
terms.definition_en: In the 31st year of Jiajing, Ming (1552), Emperor Jiajing, due to his belief in Taoism, carried out another major renovation of Wudang Mountain, building the Zhishi Xuanyue Archway and repairing the eight palaces and temples; it is the second large-scale construction in the architectural history of Wudang Mountain.

terms.term_en: Hankou Opening as a Treaty Port
terms.definition_zh: 1861年汉口根据《天津条约》开埠，成为长江中游重要的通商口岸，随后英、俄、法、德、日等国设立租界，带来了西方近代建筑风格。
terms.definition_en: In 1861, Hankou was opened as a treaty port according to the Treaty of Tientsin, becoming an important trading port in the middle reaches of the Yangtze River; subsequently, Britain, Russia, France, Germany, Japan, and other countries established concessions, bringing Western modern architectural styles.

terms.definition_zh: 近代通商口岸外国租界区内的建筑，多为西方风格，包括领事馆、洋行、银行、教堂和住宅，是中西建筑文化交流的产物。
terms.definition_en: Buildings in foreign concession areas of modern treaty ports, mostly in Western styles, including consulates, foreign firms, banks, churches, and residences, serving as products of Sino-Western architectural cultural exchange.

terms.definition_zh: 汉口开埠后设立的海关建筑，是汉口近代建筑的标志之一，融合了西方新古典主义和文艺复兴风格。
terms.definition_en: The customs house building established after Hankou opened as a treaty port, one of the landmarks of Hankou modern architecture, blending Western neoclassical and Renaissance styles.

terms.definition_zh: 西方古典建筑中柱子的样式，包括多立克、爱奥尼、科林斯、塔司干和混合柱式，是新古典主义建筑的重要元素。
terms.definition_en: The styles of columns in Western classical architecture, including Doric, Ionic, Corinthian, Tuscan, and Composite orders, serving as important elements of neoclassical architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 西方古典建筑中门廊上方的三角形装饰构件，源于古希腊神庙，新古典主义建筑中常用。
terms.definition_en: A triangular decorative component above the portico in Western classical architecture, derived from ancient Greek temples, commonly used in neoclassical architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 西方建筑中成排排列的柱子，形成柱廊，常用于建筑入口和立面，增加庄重感和层次感。
terms.definition_en: Columns arranged in rows in Western architecture, forming a colonnade, commonly used for building entrances and facades, enhancing solemnity and layering.

terms.definition_zh: 建筑外部凸出的平台，有栏杆围护，是西方近代住宅和公共建筑的常见元素，汉口近代建筑中大量出现。
terms.definition_en: A platform protruding from the exterior of a building, enclosed by railings, a common element of Western modern residences and public buildings, appearing extensively in Hankou modern architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 坡屋顶上凸出的窗户，因形似老虎张口而得名，源于西方建筑，用于阁楼采光和通风，上海和汉口近代建筑中常见。
terms.definition_en: A window protruding from a sloped roof, named for its resemblance to a tiger opening its mouth, derived from Western architecture, used for attic lighting and ventilation, commonly seen in modern buildings in Shanghai and Hankou.

terms.definition_zh: 西方近代建筑中常见的红色陶瓦屋顶，与中国传统灰瓦形成对比，汉口租界建筑中大量使用。
terms.definition_en: Red clay tile roofs common in Western modern architecture, contrasting with traditional Chinese gray tiles, extensively used in Hankou concession buildings.

terms.definition_zh: 不抹灰、直接露出砖面的砖墙，砖缝整齐，质感朴素，是西方近代建筑和中国民国时期建筑的常见做法。
terms.definition_en: A brick wall without plastering, directly exposing the brick surface, with neat brick joints and a plain texture, a common practice in Western modern architecture and Chinese Republican-period architecture.
examples: 汉口近代建筑清水砖墙

terms.definition_zh: 表面抹灰的墙面，可涂刷各种颜色，是西方近代建筑最常见的墙面处理方式。
terms.definition_en: A wall surface with plastering, paintable in various colors, the most common wall treatment in Western modern architecture.
examples: 汉口近代建筑抹灰墙面

terms.definition_zh: 柱子底部的石质基座，用于防潮和传递荷载，表面常有雕刻装饰，是中国古建筑的重要构件。
terms.definition_en: A stone base at the bottom of a column, used for moisture protection and load transfer, often with carved decorations on the surface, serving as an important component of traditional Chinese architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 大门下方的横木或石条，具有分隔空间、挡风和象征意义，中国传统建筑中门槛高低反映门第等级。
terms.definition_en: A horizontal wood or stone bar below the main gate, serving to separate spaces, block wind, and for symbolic meaning; in traditional Chinese architecture, the height of the threshold reflects the rank of the household.

terms.definition_zh: 大门两侧承托门轴的石质构件，外侧常做成抱鼓石或石狮形式，具有固定和装饰作用。
terms.definition_en: Stone components on both sides of the main gate supporting the door pivot, with the outer side often made into drum-holding stone or stone lion forms, serving fixing and decorative functions.

terms.definition_zh: 大门上的金属帽钉，既有加固门板的作用，也有装饰和等级象征意义，皇宫和高等级建筑中门钉数量有严格规定。
terms.definition_en: Metal cap nails on the main gate, serving both to reinforce the door panel and for decoration and rank symbolism; in imperial palaces and high-grade buildings, the number of door nails is strictly regulated.

terms.definition_zh: 大门上的金属门环底座，常做成兽面或环形，用于叩门和装饰，中国传统建筑中常见。
terms.definition_en: A metal door-ring base on the main gate, often made into animal-face or ring shapes, used for knocking and decoration, commonly seen in traditional Chinese architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 悬挂于门楣或殿堂上方的题字板，多为木质或石质，书写建筑名称或吉祥语，是中国古建筑的重要标识。
terms.definition_en: An inscribed board hung above a lintel or hall, mostly wooden or stone, inscribed with the building name or auspicious phrases, serving as an important identifier of traditional Chinese architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 悬挂或镌刻于柱子上的对联，多为木质或石质，书写对仗工整的诗句，是中国古建筑的文化装饰。
terms.definition_en: Couplets hung or engraved on columns, mostly wooden or stone, inscribed with neatly antithetical verses, serving as cultural decorations of traditional Chinese architecture.

terms.definition_zh: 刻有文字的石质碑刻，用于记录历史事件、人物事迹和建筑修缮，是研究古建筑历史的重要实物资料。
terms.definition_en: Stone steles engraved with text, used to record historical events, person deeds, and building renovations, serving as important physical materials for studying the history of ancient buildings.

terms.definition_zh: 塔顶部的装饰构件，通常由刹座、刹杆、相轮、宝盖和宝珠组成，是佛塔的标志性部件。
terms.definition_en: A decorative component at the top of a pagoda, usually composed of a finial base, finial pole, ring disks, canopy, and jewel, serving as the iconic part of a Buddhist pagoda.

terms.definition_zh: 塔刹上的环状部件，层层叠叠，是佛塔的重要装饰和象征，相轮数量反映塔的等级。
terms.definition_en: Ring-shaped components on the pagoda finial, stacked in layers, serving as important decorations and symbols of Buddhist pagodas; the number of ring disks reflects the grade of the pagoda.

terms.definition_zh: 佛塔基下的地下空间，用于安放舍利和珍贵文物，是佛塔的重要组成部分。
terms.definition_en: An underground space beneath the foundation of a Buddhist pagoda, used to enshrine relics and precious cultural relics, serving as an important part of Buddhist pagodas.

terms.definition_zh: 以石、木、铜等材料雕刻或铸造的宗教神像，是寺庙和石窟中的核心供奉对象。
terms.definition_en: Religious deity statues carved or cast in stone, wood, bronze, and other materials, serving as the core objects of worship in temples and grottoes.
